hints: Look closely at R first. It shows a central star of xylem with separate patches of phloem between the arms, quite different from the other three diagrams.

Remember the three classic patterns: root has alternating xylem and phloem in the centre, stem has side-by-side bundles with phloem outside and xylem inside, leaf midrib has xylem on top (toward upper epidermis) and phloem below.
walkthrough:
**Spot the root in R**

Start with the easiest one. R shows a solid central core where xylem forms a 4-armed cross with phloem sitting in the gaps between the arms.

This alternating, central arrangement is the classic dicot root stele. So R = root.

**Spot the two stem bundles in Q and T**

Now look at Q and T. Both show a small discrete bundle with phloem on the outside (closest to the epidermis) and xylem on the inside (furthest from the epidermis).

This side-by-side, conjoint arrangement with outer phloem and inner xylem is typical of a stem vascular bundle. So Q = stem and T = stem.

**Spot the leaf in S**

Finally look at S. It is a large crescent shape under the upper epidermis, with xylem on the upper side and phloem on the lower side.

In a leaf midrib, xylem is adaxial (upper, to supply water for photosynthesis) and phloem is abaxial (lower). So S = leaf.

Putting it together: Q stem, R root, S leaf, T stem, which matches option D.

options.A: Q is not a leaf and S is not a stem. Q shows outer phloem and inner xylem of a stem bundle, while S shows upper xylem and lower phloem of a leaf.
options.B: Q is not a root and R is not a stem. R with central alternating xylem and phloem is a root, while Q with conjoint outer phloem is a stem.
options.C: R is not a stem and T is not a root. R is the alternating root stele, while T is a conjoint stem bundle just like Q.
options.D: Correct. Q stem (phloem outside, xylem inside), R root (central alternating stele), S leaf (upper xylem, lower phloem), T stem (phloem outside, xylem inside).
